$comment: The single scripted two-turn session test/eval-teach-me-testing.js drives against a real vendor.
Turn 1 runs the whole first-session path through the real bmad-teach-me-testing skill, playing both
the facilitator and the learner: role, experience level, learning goals, session selection, a
deliberately wrong answer to session-01's own Q1, the below-70% [R]/[C] review branch, and exit.
Turn 2 is a fresh, memoryless process that proves progress persistence is real rather than assumed --
see the story spec's Design Notes for why a single-turn design could not tell a correct write from a
skill that would forget everything the instant the process exited.
Every value below that describes the real skill's own wording is cross-checked in validateCorpus
against the live step files and data files it names, the same discipline test/eval-nfr.js's
skillRuleCitations applies: a claim this corpus rests a score on has to still be true of the skill on
disk, so a later edit to the real workflow fails this corpus before it silently miscalibrates a live
run.
correctionPhrase is step-04-session-01.md's own verbatim text for an incorrect answer to session-01's
Q1 (q1-purpose in data/quiz-questions.yaml), pinned as the containment token for two separate checks:
correctionHolds asks whether it appears at all in turn 1's transcript (the seeded misconception being
corrected the first time), and reTeachingHolds asks whether it appears AGAIN after reviewMarker (the
same content actually being re-taught when the learner chooses to review, rather than the review
silently reusing the transcript's own earlier occurrence).
quizAnswers scripts exactly one wrong answer (q1-purpose) against the real answer key in
data/quiz-questions.yaml, landing at 2/3 = 66.67%, below the file's own 70% passing_score, which is
what puts the session on the [R]/[C] branch at all. quizQuestionEvidence is what masteryClaimHolds
cross-references a completed session's claim against: session-01-quickstart's own Q1 question text,
unique to that session, so a progress.yaml claiming a DIFFERENT session complete with no matching
evidence in the transcript is caught as an unearned mastery claim rather than passed by a marker
generic enough to appear in any session's quiz.
continuationMarker and freshStartMarker are step-01-init.md's own two mutually exclusive greetings:
turn 2 must land on the continuation branch (having found turn 1's progress file), never the fresh-
start branch, which is the structural proof that persistence is real rather than assumed.
learningGoals: Learn testing fundamentals well enough to start contributing automated coverage at work.
correctionPhrase: TEA's purpose is to make testing expertise accessible through structured workflows and knowledge (B)

quizQuestionEvidence.session-01-quickstart: What is the primary purpose of TEA?
